rework.closure:
Corrected the mechanism in both surfaces; the practical instruction and the observation are preserved.

docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md:396-410 now reads:
- **Issue one configuration save after a fixture edit.** After changing a
  provider fixture, issue one configuration save (the post-save trigger) rather
  than relying on the scheduled reconciliation task alone. The reason is the
  ADR-022 durable reconciliation cursor, not cache staleness: a scheduled (or
  post-scan) run resumes from the persisted cursor anchor and covers the library
  round-robin across successive runs, so a single scheduled run is not
  guaranteed to re-cover an edited item, while the post-save trigger is
  deliberately excluded from the cursor and always enumerates from the start
  (ADR-022 clause 6). Every reconciliation, including a scheduled one, already
  invalidates the provider inventory at the top of its run (ADR-018 clause 3),
  so the pre-edit observation was not served from the inventory cache. In this
  run a scheduled task after the edit still produced
  `RenderPassThrough (PassThroughReason=NoDisplayableValue)` for the sparse
  movie, and the changed record was published only after the additional save,
  so a verifier could wrongly conclude that changed metadata does not republish.

docs/implementation/21.9/live-verification.json F-21.9-6 detail, part (2), now reads:
(2) The procedure does not say that after a provider-fixture edit the verifier must issue one configuration save before expecting the scheduled reconciliation task to cover the change. The scheduled run resumes from the persisted ADR-022 durable reconciliation cursor anchor and covers the library round-robin across successive runs, so it is not guaranteed to re-cover the edited item, while the post-save trigger is deliberately excluded from the cursor and always enumerates from the start (ADR-022 clause 6). A verifier who edits a provider fixture and only runs the scheduled task can therefore see the changed record remain unpublished and wrongly conclude that changed metadata does not republish. This is not provider-inventory-cache staleness: every reconciliation, including the scheduled one, discards the retained observation sets unconditionally (ADR-018 clause 3; LibraryReconciliationService.ReconcileAsync calls InvalidateInventory()).

F-21.9-6 evidence bullet 2 now reads:
In this run, after editing the verifier's own radarr/moviefile.json to give the sparse movie a file record, the scheduled task at 15:20:23Z did not re-render the sparse item (it still produced 'RenderPassThrough (PassThroughReason=NoDisplayableValue)'), and the change only became visible after an additional configuration save (the post-save trigger) at 15:21:40Z, which published the sparse item. The scheduled run cannot have served a cached pre-edit provider observation: every reconciliation discards the retained observation sets unconditionally (src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/LibraryReconciliationService.cs:139 calls InvalidateInventory(), ADR-018 clause 3), asserted for PostScan, Scheduled and PostSave by tests/ArrTags.Tests/ReconciliationTriggerTests.cs:254 (ReconciliationInvalidatesTheInventoryForEverySource). The consistent explanation is the ADR-022 durable reconciliation cursor, which governs only scheduled and post-scan runs (LibraryReconciliationService.cs:151 sets usesCursor for Scheduled or PostScan): a scheduled run resumes from the persisted anchor and covers the library round-robin across successive runs, while the post-save trigger always enumerates from the start and leaves the cursor untouched (docs/decisions/ADR-022.md:105-113, clause 6).

F-21.9-6 evidence bullet 3 now reads:
docs/implementation/14.3/live-verification.json records for the v1.1 run that every reconciliation discards the retained observation sets (LibraryReconciliationService.InvalidateInventory) and that the post-save and library-refresh windows each produced fresh provider reads, i.e. per-reconciliation invalidation, not a save needed to refresh a stale inventory cache.

F-21.9-6 recommended_action now reads:
In the v1.2 section of docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md, state that the plugin must be configured only through POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration (never by hand-editing ArrTags.xml) and that after editing a provider fixture the verifier must issue one configuration save, whose post-save reconciliation always enumerates from the start and therefore covers the change, because a scheduled run resumes from the persisted ADR-022 cursor anchor and only covers the library round-robin across successive runs. Do not attribute the need for the save to provider-inventory-cache staleness: every reconciliation, including a scheduled one, invalidates the inventory (ADR-018 clause 3).

New F-21.9-6 correction field:
R-21.9-1 (MEDIUM, attempt-2 rework): the original F-21.9-6 detail and evidence attributed the post-fixture-edit stale observation to the provider inventory cache still serving the pre-edit read. The implementation contradicts that mechanism - LibraryReconciliationService.ReconcileAsync calls InvalidateInventory() unconditionally at the top of every run (src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/LibraryReconciliationService.cs:139), and ReconciliationInvalidatesTheInventoryForEverySource asserts PostScan, Scheduled and PostSave each discard the retained observation sets (tests/ArrTags.Tests/ReconciliationTriggerTests.cs:254) - so the causal attribution was corrected to the ADR-022 durable reconciliation cursor (scheduled/post-scan resume from the persisted anchor and cover the library round-robin; the post-save trigger always enumerates from the start). The underlying observation and the practical procedure instruction (issue one configuration save after a fixture edit) are unchanged.

The 'UNCHANGED vs CHANGED METADATA' note now reads:
UNCHANGED vs CHANGED METADATA. Unchanged provider metadata did not republish: two further scheduled-task triggers with the fixture untouched left both owned items' persisted ActiveImageIdentity and served bytes byte-identical. Changed provider metadata did republish: adding a movie-file record for the sparse movie produced a fresh 'Published: The derived artwork was published and committed.' with a new ActiveImageIdentity. The sparse movie was not re-rendered by the scheduled run after the edit; establishing the change required one configuration save, because the post-save trigger always enumerates from the start while the scheduled run resumes from the persisted ADR-022 cursor anchor and covers the library round-robin across successive runs (every reconciliation, including the scheduled one, already invalidates the provider inventory, ADR-018 clause 3) - see F-21.9-6.
